declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartII.actual_infinite_state_is_measurable
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_infinite_state_is_measurable (k goal sigma : ℝ) (t : ℕ) :
    Measurable (fun w : ℕ → ℝ => infiniteTrajectory k goal sigma w t)
declarations.body_review: Induction on the literal primitive recursive trajectory uses measurable coordinate projections and real sums/products. This is ordinary Measurable, resolving the earlier distinction from publicly exported HasLaw/AEMeasurable.

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartII.actual_infinite_positive_time_state_has_the_existing_standard_deviation_law
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_infinite_positive_time_state_has_the_existing_standard_deviation_law
    (k goal sigma : ℝ) (t : ℕ) :
    HasLaw (fun w : ℕ → ℝ => infiniteTrajectory k goal sigma w t)
      (gaussianReal (trueMean k goal t) ((stateSD k sigma t)^2)) infiniteNoiseLaw
declarations.body_review: The actual infinite marginal law is rewritten using stateSD=NNReal.sqrt(trueVariance.toNNReal) and sq_sqrt. It holds at every natural time despite its name; at time zero it correctly gives the degenerate Gaussian. The state's SD is not confused with the recurrence noise scale.

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartII.the_printed_standardized_event_is_pointwise_the_original_infinite_state_event
declarations.signature:
theorem the_printed_standardized_event_is_pointwise_the_original_infinite_state_event
    (k goal sigma : ℝ) (t : ℕ) (hv : 0 < trueVariance k sigma t) (w : ℕ → ℝ) :
    (1 < infiniteTrajectory k goal sigma w t) ↔
      ((1-trueMean k goal t)/Real.sqrt (trueVariance k sigma t) <
        (infiniteTrajectory k goal sigma w t-trueMean k goal t)/Real.sqrt (trueVariance k sigma t))
declarations.body_review: At positive true variance, the real square root is positive. Positive-denominator division and common translation prove both event directions for every w. It is the actual same infinite state, not an assumed standardized random variable.

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartII.actual_standardized_infinite_positive_time_state_has_standard_gaussian_law
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_standardized_infinite_positive_time_state_has_standard_gaussian_law
    (k goal sigma : ℝ) (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t) (hsigma : sigma ≠ 0) :
    HasLaw (fun w : ℕ → ℝ =>
      (infiniteTrajectory k goal sigma w t-trueMean k goal t)/Real.sqrt (trueVariance k sigma t))
      (gaussianReal 0 1) infiniteNoiseLaw
declarations.body_review: Actual infinite state HasLaw is derived, then subtraction/scaling of Gaussian laws is used. Positive time and nonzero noise give nonzero stateSD; its square is exactly the NNReal scaling variance, so variance division gives one and centered mean gives zero. Real.sqrt matches the NNReal SD representation. No target normalized-law hypothesis is assumed.

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartII.actual_infinite_one_based_failure_probability_is_the_true_piecewise_tail
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_infinite_one_based_failure_probability_is_the_true_piecewise_tail
    (k goal sigma : ℝ) (T : ℕ) (t : Fin T) :
    infiniteNoiseLaw.real {w | 1 < infiniteTrajectory k goal sigma w (t.val+1)} =
      exactTail k goal sigma (t.val+1)
declarations.body_review: Actual finite-prefix HasLaw transfers the measurable finite-state event. Literal prefix agreement identifies the state at t.val+1; an explicit set identity replaces the event before applying the existing finite piecewise-tail theorem. Fin T means exactly times one through T, and the T=0 case has no indices.

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartII.actual_infinite_violation_count_is_the_finite_prefix_count_pointwise
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_infinite_violation_count_is_the_finite_prefix_count_pointwise
    (k goal sigma : ℝ) (T : ℕ) (w : ℕ → ℝ) :
    infiniteViolationCount k goal sigma T w =
      violationCount k goal sigma (fun j : Fin T => w j.val)
declarations.body_review: The newly defined infiniteViolationCount equals the existing violationCount pulled back by the Fin T prefix projection for each w. Both sum the same strict indicator at t.val+1. The recurrence prefix equality has the justified bound t.val+1<=T; no noise after the finite horizon enters.

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartII.actual_infinite_violation_count_is_integrable
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_infinite_violation_count_is_integrable
    (k goal sigma : ℝ) (T : ℕ) :
    Integrable (infiniteViolationCount k goal sigma T) infiniteNoiseLaw
declarations.body_review: A finite sum of indicator functions is integrable under the normalized infinite Gaussian measure. Each event is ordinarily measurable by the new state measurability theorem; no unproved AEMeasurable upgrade or independent-state premise is used.

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartII.actual_one_to_T_infinite_indicator_expectation_is_the_sum_of_its_marginal_probabilities
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_one_to_T_infinite_indicator_expectation_is_the_sum_of_its_marginal_probabilities
    (k goal sigma : ℝ) (T : ℕ) :
    (∫ w, infiniteViolationCount k goal sigma T w ∂infiniteNoiseLaw) =
      ∑ t : Fin T, infiniteNoiseLaw.real {w | 1 < infiniteTrajectory k goal sigma w (t.val+1)}
declarations.body_review: Direct integral_finsetSum on the infinite noise space is justified by integrability of each measurable bounded indicator. integral_indicator_one produces its actual event probability. No state independence appears among the hypotheses.

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartII.actual_one_to_T_infinite_count_expectation_is_the_printed_piecewise_tail_sum
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_one_to_T_infinite_count_expectation_is_the_printed_piecewise_tail_sum
    (k goal sigma : ℝ) (T : ℕ) :
    (∫ w, infiniteViolationCount k goal sigma T w ∂infiniteNoiseLaw) =
      ∑ t : Fin T, exactTail k goal sigma (t.val+1)
declarations.body_review: Actual infinite count expectation is first identified with its true one-based marginal probabilities, then the finite-prefix-derived probability theorem gives exactTail. The formula holds for arbitrary real parameters and all T, including sigma=0 and T=0.

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartII.actual_positive_noise_one_to_T_infinite_count_expectation_is_the_printed_erfc_sum
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_positive_noise_one_to_T_infinite_count_expectation_is_the_printed_erfc_sum
    (k goal sigma : ℝ) (T : ℕ) (hsigma : sigma ≠ 0) :
    (∫ w, infiniteViolationCount k goal sigma T w ∂infiniteNoiseLaw) =
      ∑ t : Fin T, (1/2:ℝ)*erfc
        (((1-trueMean k goal (t.val+1))/Real.sqrt (trueVariance k sigma (t.val+1)))/Real.sqrt 2)
declarations.body_review: The hypothesis is sigma!=0, stronger in scope than the printed sigma>0 case despite the theorem name. This selects the nondegenerate branch, then genuine CDF-complement/density and erfc change-of-variable identities transform each summand. The real erfc sum has no floating-point implementation or accuracy claim.

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartII.actual_zero_noise_infinite_count_uses_strict_mean_indicators_and_boundary_equality_is_safe
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_zero_noise_infinite_count_uses_strict_mean_indicators_and_boundary_equality_is_safe
    (k goal : ℝ) (T : ℕ) :
    (∫ w, infiniteViolationCount k goal 0 T w ∂infiniteNoiseLaw) =
      ∑ t : Fin T, (if 1 < trueMean k goal (t.val+1) then 1 else 0) ∧
    ∀ t : Fin T, trueMean k goal (t.val+1) = 1 →
      infiniteNoiseLaw.real {w | 1 < infiniteTrajectory k goal 0 w (t.val+1)} = 0
declarations.body_review: At zero noise the expectation is the sum of strict trueMean indicators; each mean equal to one gives zero actual infinite-state violation probability. For the general per-time indicator formula also cite the public infinite piecewise probability theorem; a summed expectation alone is not treated as an individual probability statement.

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartII.actual_zero_noise_has_zero_variance_and_zero_standardizing_denominator
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_zero_noise_has_zero_variance_and_zero_standardizing_denominator
    (k : ℝ) (t : ℕ) :
    trueVariance k 0 t = 0 ∧ Real.sqrt (trueVariance k 0 t) = 0
declarations.body_review: The actual trueVariance definition specializes to zero and its real square root is zero at all times. This breaks the method's positive-variance precondition; it does not claim Lean real division is undefined. The separate deterministic probability branch prevents substituting Q(0)=1/2.

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartII.actual_time_zero_is_safe_and_zero_horizon_has_zero_count_expectation
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_time_zero_is_safe_and_zero_horizon_has_zero_count_expectation
    (k goal sigma : ℝ) :
    (∀ w : ℕ → ℝ, infiniteTrajectory k goal sigma w 0 = 0) ∧
    infiniteNoiseLaw.real {w | 1 < infiniteTrajectory k goal sigma w 0} = 0 ∧
    (∫ w, infiniteViolationCount k goal sigma 0 w ∂infiniteNoiseLaw) = 0
declarations.body_review: The literal path starts at zero for every w, its strict upper-one event is empty with probability zero, and the empty Fin 0 count has zero expectation. These conclusions hold for all real parameters, including nonzero noise.

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartII.actual_nonzero_noise_positive_horizon_count_is_positive_so_a_rounded_zero_cannot_certify_zero_cost
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_nonzero_noise_positive_horizon_count_is_positive_so_a_rounded_zero_cannot_certify_zero_cost
    (k goal sigma : ℝ) (T : ℕ) (hT : 0 < T) (hsigma : sigma ≠ 0) :
    0 < (∫ w, infiniteViolationCount k goal sigma T w ∂infiniteNoiseLaw)
declarations.body_review: All true marginal probabilities are nonnegative and the first one-based event has strictly positive probability for sigma!=0. A nonempty Fin T sum is therefore positive when T>0. The endpoint proves only positivity of the true expectation. It implies rejection of the exact zero budget, but does not prove existence or accuracy of any rounded display, CDF rounding or underflow model.
